title: Mix the layered solution in two open test tubes without spilling it
instruction: Mix the solution in each test tube, then stand the tubes back in the rack.
context: Mixing an open test tube is routine work for lab technicians and teaching-lab staff. The tubes hold 0.5 M copper(II) sulfate (causes serious eye damage) with no stoppers. The layers mix only under brisk agitation, but turned over, tipped past about 85 degrees or shaken hard the open tube throws liquid out. The robot must find agitation that mixes yet keeps the liquid in, for two tubes, then rack them.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y left, z up); arms start in the ready pose; the layout is the same in every trial. Rack: green polypropylene test-tube rack, 6 x 24 cm, centred at x 26, y 0, clamped or taped to the bench: a 1.2 cm base board; a 1 cm top board whose top is 7 cm above the table, with two 25 mm square holes at y +8 and -8; a 1.2 cm end post at each end; open under the top board. Tubes (2): borosilicate glass test tubes, 16 mm outside, 14 mm bore, 100 mm long (9.5 g), open (no stoppers), standing in the two holes on the base board, mouths 11.2 cm above the table. In each tube: 2 mL of 0.5 M copper(II) sulfate solution (dark blue, 13 mm deep) with 2 mL of water carefully layered on top (13 mm); the liquid's surface is 72 mm below the mouth. Nothing else on the table. The screenshot's inset is the left wrist camera's view of a lifted tube before mixing (clear water over dark blue).
scoring: Spill (latched for the whole trial): 0 once liquid reaches the mouth of either tube. Otherwise 0.25 per tube mixed; 0.5 both mixed but not both racked and released; 0.75 both mixed, both standing in their own holes (the tube passes through its hole, its axis crossing the top board within 6 mm of the hole's centre, bottom on the base board within 8 mm, leaning 20 degrees or less), every gripper pad and tool point 3 cm or more from both tubes, tubes still; success (1.0) once that has held 1 s. Real trial, measured directly: spill = a tube loses 0.05 g or more (weighed on a 0.01 g balance before and after) or any blue spot on the white absorbent paper covering the bench (60 x 60 cm), the rack or the arms; mixed = in a photo against a white card, the mean red channel of 3 x 3 mm patches at a quarter and three quarters of the liquid's height differ by 10% or less of the larger (a freshly layered tube differs by about 70%). In simulation both are computed by the liquid model from the tube's motion (README).
reset_notes: Empty, rinse and dry the tubes. Refill each with 2 mL of 0.5 M copper(II) sulfate solution, then layer 2 mL of water on top slowly down the wall with a dropping pipette (or use dyed sugar solution under water, README); weigh each tube in the rack. Replace the white bench paper if marked.
fidelity: Approximate. Tubes are PhysX rigid bodies, the rack fixed boxes. There is no liquid simulation: a reduced-order model (first sloshing mode, exact wall height, column lift), stepped at 240 Hz from each tube's pose, latches a spill when the liquid reaches the mouth and counts mixing strokes. Its 30-degree stroke threshold and 25% mixing per stroke are chosen, not measured; the real trial measures spills and colour directly. Details in README.
